titles.t: Hundreds Leave Russian-Occupied Oleshky During an 80-Hour Ceasefire
Melania Trump Brokered a Ceasefire in Oleshky. Here Is What Happened
Inside the Oleshky Evacuation: Aid, Convoys and an 80-Hour Truce
How Ukraine and Russia Agreed to Open Oleshky for Civilians
Oleshky Residents Got a Choice. Most Reportedly Picked Ukraine
Melania Trump's Oleshky Deal: A Rare Truce Putin's Side Signed
Can the Oleshky Ceasefire Become a Model Along the Front?
Oleshky After 80 Hours of Quiet: What the Evacuation Proves
Russia Occupied Oleshky. Given the Chance, Its People Left
RT Shows Up in Oleshky With a Story. The Evacuees Tell Another
Oleshky Shows What Russian Occupation Really Costs Ukrainians
An 80-Hour Truce in Oleshky Exposed Putin's Occupation

descs.t: Hundreds of civilians were evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine during a rare local ceasefire that has held for 80 hours. Russian and Ukrainian humanitarian commissioners delivered aid and opened corridors in a mission coordinated by First Lady Melania Trump. We walk through how the evacuation worked and where residents chose to go.

A local ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky let aid in and residents out, with both sides crediting Melania Trump for brokering it. Reports say far more evacuees chose Ukraine than Russia. We look at what this truce achieved, what it did not, and whether missions like it could become regular along the front.

Russia occupied Oleshky, and when an 80-hour ceasefire finally gave its residents a choice, reports say most of them chose Ukraine. Melania Trump helped broker the truce, aid reached the town, and RT arrived with its own version of events. Here is what the evacuation reveals about life under Russian occupation.

intro.plain: Something rare happened in southern Ukraine. A local ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky has held for 80 hours, aid got in, and hundreds of civilians were evacuated. Both Ukrainian and Russian officials are thanking Melania Trump for brokering it. Chat: should missions like this become regular along the front?
intro.mid: Oleshky has been under Russian occupation, and for 80 hours the guns went quiet so residents could leave. Hundreds did, and reports say far more chose Ukraine than Russia. Melania Trump helped broker the deal. Is this a crack that leads to more, or a one-off? Chat, what do you think comes next?
intro.bold: Give people under Russian occupation a free choice, and look what they do. In Oleshky, an 80-hour truce opened the road, and reports say most evacuees headed for Ukraine. Meanwhile RT showed up to spin it. Chat, what does that choice tell you about Putin's so-called liberation?

hook.plain: For 80 hours, the fighting around Russian-occupied Oleshky stopped, and hundreds of civilians walked out. Here is how the ceasefire was arranged.
hook.mid: Russian and Ukrainian officials agreed on something: a truce in Oleshky. Here is what it delivered, and who made it happen.
hook.bold: Russia occupied Oleshky. The moment residents got a safe road out, reports say most chose Ukraine. Here is what they left behind.

titles.t: IRGC Says Three Tankers Are Burning in the Strait of Hormuz
Limpet Mines in Hormuz: A Third Tanker Hit in One Day
What We Know About the Hormuz Tanker Attacks So Far
How the IRGC Is Hitting Tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
IRGC Punishes 'Unauthorized' Routes as CENTCOM Says Oil Flows
Is the IRGC Switching to Limpet Mines in Hormuz?
CENTCOM Says Hormuz Is Open. The IRGC Says Otherwise
Six Months to Clear the Mines: What Hormuz Means for Oil
CENTCOM Says Its Navy Is Gone. Now the IRGC Plants Mines
The Regime Is Setting Tankers on FIRE in Hormuz
Piracy by a Regime: The IRGC's War on Hormuz Shipping
Why the IRGC's Tanker Attacks Show a Regime Running Out of Moves

descs.t: The IRGC Navy says three tankers have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and says it is punishing ships that use unauthorized routes. UKMTO and security sources report limpet mines attached to a tanker overnight. We go through what is reported, what the IRGC claims, and what CENTCOM says about shipping.

Three tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, by the IRGC's own account, while CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper says ships are flowing and the regime's oil exports are at zero. The Financial Times calls the limpet mine attacks an apparent tactical shift. We look at both claims and what it means for oil and for the war.

The IRGC is boasting about burning tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, after reports that its boats attached limpet mines to a ship in the protected lane. CENTCOM says the regime's navy is destroyed and its oil exports are at zero. We break down why sneak attacks on shipping are what a cornered regime does.

intro.plain: The IRGC Navy says three tankers have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and it says it is punishing ships that use unauthorized routes. Security sources report limpet mines attached to at least one tanker. At the same time CENTCOM says ships are flowing again. Chat, which side do you believe on Hormuz right now?
intro.mid: Two stories about the Strait of Hormuz today, and they do not match. CENTCOM's Admiral Cooper says ships are flowing and the regime's oil exports are at zero. The IRGC says three tankers are on fire. The FT calls the limpet mines a tactical shift. Chat, is Hormuz open or not?
intro.bold: The IRGC is putting out videos of tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz and calling it punishment. Reports say its boats slipped into the protected lane and stuck limpet mines on a ship. CENTCOM says the regime's navy is destroyed. Chat, is this a regime fighting back or one running out of moves?

hook.plain: Three tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, by the IRGC's own count. Here is what is reported, how the attacks were carried out, and what it means for shipping.
hook.mid: CENTCOM says Hormuz is open. The IRGC says three tankers are burning. Here is how both can be true, and what it does to oil.
hook.bold: With its navy reportedly destroyed, the IRGC is sticking mines on tankers. Here is what that tells you about a regime under pressure.

titles.t: Rahul Gandhi Says Modi Sold IDBI Bank at a Throwaway Price
Sitharaman Hits Back Over the IDBI Bank Sale
The IDBI Bank Sale Fight: Each Side's Claim Checked
Why Congress and the Modi Government Are Fighting Over IDBI
Throwaway Price or a Lie? The Battle Over IDBI Bank
Sitharaman Drags Up 1957 to Answer Rahul Gandhi on IDBI
Should a Government Own a Bank at All? The IDBI Debate
IDBI Bank: What the Sale Says About State Run Banking
Congress Defends State Banks. That Is the REAL Problem
Selling IDBI Bank Is Not the Scandal. Owning It Was
Why Politicians Love State Banks: The IDBI Fight Explained
Loans on a Minister's Whim: The Case Against State Banks

descs.t: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi says the Modi government sold IDBI Bank at a throwaway price. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says Congress has long used banks and financial institutions as personal entities, and government supporters call his claim a lie. We go through what each side says about the IDBI Bank sale.

The IDBI Bank sale has become a fight over history. Rahul Gandhi calls it a sale at a throwaway price, Nirmala Sitharaman answers with Congress's record of pressuring bank staff to lend, and Congress says it stands with IDBI employees. We look at the claims and the bigger question of who should own a bank.

Rahul Gandhi is attacking the sale of IDBI Bank, while the Finance Minister says Congress treated banks as personal entities and pushed staff to lend on a whim. We make the case that the scandal is a government owning a bank in the first place, and look at what each side claims about the sale.

intro.plain: There is a fight over the sale of IDBI Bank. Rahul Gandhi says the Modi government sold it at a throwaway price. Nirmala Sitharaman says Congress used banks as personal entities and pressured staff to hand out loans. Supporters of the government call his claim a lie. Chat, should governments be running banks at all?
intro.mid: Rahul Gandhi says IDBI Bank was sold off cheap. The Finance Minister answers with a history lesson on how Congress used banks, and Congress says it stands with IDBI employees. The real question underneath is who should own a bank. Chat, government or private, which do you trust with your money?
intro.bold: Rahul Gandhi is angry that IDBI Bank was sold. I think the real scandal is that a government ever ran it. The Finance Minister says Congress pressured bank staff to lend on a whim. That is exactly what happens when politicians own banks. Chat, agree or disagree?

hook.plain: Rahul Gandhi says IDBI Bank went for a throwaway price. The government says that is a lie. Here is what each side claims.
hook.mid: A bank sale has turned into a fight over decades of history. Here is the IDBI row, and the question nobody is asking.
hook.bold: When politicians own banks, loans follow politics. The IDBI fight shows why, and here is the case for getting government out.

Paxton vs Talarico: Reading the Final Texas Senate Poll
What a One Point Gap Means for the Texas Senate Seat
Could Democrats Really Flip Texas? The Last Poll Says Maybe
Elon Musk Tells Texas to Vote Paxton as Talarico Closes In
Texas Senate: Why Abbott Leads by 6 and Paxton Only by 1
The Texas Seat That Could Tip Control of the US Senate
One POINT: Texas Is Closer Than Anyone Expected
Talarico's Healthcare Pitch vs Paxton: Texas Decides Now
Every Vote Counts in Texas This Time, and Here Is Why
Texas on a Knife Edge: What a Talarico Upset Would Change

descs.t: The final Texas Senate poll from Quantus has Ken Paxton at 49.4 percent and James Talarico at 48.4 percent as early voting ends. The same poll has Greg Abbott ahead of Gina Hinojosa 52 to 46 for governor. We go through the numbers and what they say about turnout in Texas.

Ken Paxton leads James Talarico by one point in the final Texas Senate poll, while Greg Abbott leads by six for governor. Elon Musk has urged his followers to vote Paxton, and Talarico is running on healthcare for all. We look at why the Senate race is so much closer than the governor's race and what it means for control of the Senate.

Texas is one point from a Senate upset. The final Quantus poll has Ken Paxton at 49.4 percent and James Talarico at 48.4, with early voting closing and both sides pushing every last voter. We break down the race, the gap with the governor's contest, and what a Talarico win would mean.

intro.plain: The final Texas Senate poll is in: Ken Paxton 49.4 percent, James Talarico 48.4. That is one point, with early voting closing. For governor, Abbott leads Hinojosa by six. So the Senate race is the one to watch. Chat, are you in Texas, and did you vote early?
intro.mid: Texas, of all places, has a one point Senate race. Paxton 49.4, Talarico 48.4 in the final Quantus poll, while Abbott leads the governor's race by six. Elon Musk is telling his followers to vote Paxton. So why is Paxton running so far behind Abbott? Chat, give me your theory.
intro.bold: One point. That is all that separates Ken Paxton and James Talarico in the final Texas Senate poll, and early voting is closing. A Democrat winning a Texas Senate seat would shake up the whole map. Chat, call it now: does Paxton hold Texas or does Talarico pull the upset?

hook.plain: Paxton 49.4, Talarico 48.4. The final Texas Senate poll is a one point race. Here is what the numbers say and where the votes could still move.
hook.mid: Abbott leads Texas by six. Paxton leads by one. That gap tells you a lot about this Senate race, and here is what it means.
hook.bold: Texas is one point from a Senate upset. Here is how the race got this close, and what happens if it flips.

Decoy Dan: What the DOJ Must Prove Before Alaska Votes
Two Dan Sullivans, One Senate Seat: Who Gains From the Confusion

Peltola's Campaign, the DSCC and the Decoy: Follow the Trail

descs.t: Alaska's Senate race now has a criminal investigation attached to it: the US Attorney in Alaska and FBI Anchorage say they are pursuing both a criminal and a civil case over a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot. Mary Peltola denies knowing about any plot. We walk through what the New York Times reported, what the DOJ said, and what Alaska voters told reporters.

Mary Peltola says she knew nothing about the second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot, while the New York Times reports her staff spent months recruiting him and kept her updated. Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered a state criminal investigation and the DOJ wants certification blocked. Here is what each side claims and what would decide the race.

A second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's ballot, a candidate who reportedly never campaigned, and now the FBI, the DOJ and the governor all investigating. Mary Peltola denies any part in it; the New York Times reporting says her campaign and the DSCC were involved. We lay out the evidence, the denials and what it means for a Senate seat days before the vote.

intro.plain: Alaska's Senate race now has the FBI in it. The US Attorney in Anchorage says there is a criminal case and a civil case over a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, and Mary Peltola says she knew nothing. Voters told reporters they are not confused at all. So, chat: does a name trick like this actually change votes?
intro.mid: Mary Peltola says she knew nothing about the second Dan Sullivan. The New York Times reports her staff spent months recruiting him and kept her updated. The governor has ordered a criminal investigation and the DOJ wants certification blocked. Days before the vote, this is now about who runs Alaska's Senate seat. Chat: should the state hold certification until the probe ends?
intro.bold: A decoy candidate, a real senator with the same name, and now the FBI. Reports say Peltola's campaign and the DSCC helped put a second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's ballot, a man who reportedly never held a single event and now cannot be found. Peltola denies all of it. Chat, tell me straight: is this a dirty trick or a crime?

hook.plain: There are two Dan Sullivans on Alaska's Senate ballot, and federal prosecutors now say they are investigating how the second one got there. Here is what they confirmed.
hook.mid: Mary Peltola says she knew nothing. The New York Times says her staff kept her updated for months. Here is the evidence on both sides.
hook.bold: The second Dan Sullivan never campaigned, and now nobody can find him. The FBI is looking. Here is who reportedly put him on the ballot.

Why Flávio Bolsonaro Left Brazil After Losing the Election
Brazil's Election Result, the Fraud Claim and Washington's Answer
Bolsonaro Expected Trump's Help. Sources Say He Will Not Get It
Lula Won the Second Round. The Bolsonaro Camp Says It Was Stolen
What Flávio Bolsonaro Loses When His Immunity Runs Out
How Lula Won It Back: The Southeast Swing That Decided Brazil
Flávio Bolsonaro Bet on Trump. Trump Is Walking Away
Lost the Vote, Fled the Country: The Bolsonaro Playbook Again
A Stolen Election or a Sore Loser? Brazil's Claim Put to the Test
Congress Wants to Know Why Flávio Bolsonaro Is in America

descs.t: Sources say President Trump is not planning to back Flávio Bolsonaro's claim to be Brazil's rightful leader after he lost the presidential runoff to Lula and left for the United States. We walk through the result, the fraud claim, and what US officials and lawmakers are saying.

Flávio Bolsonaro says Brazil's election was stolen; Lula won the second round on big swings in the Southeast and Goiás. Now sources say Trump will not back his claim, Democrats in Congress are opening a probe into his stay in the US, and he is set to lose his parliamentary immunity next year. Here is what that means for him and for Brazil.

Flávio Bolsonaro lost Brazil's presidential election, called it stolen and left for America, the same road his father took. The man he counted on, Donald Trump, reportedly will not back him. We look at the fraud claim, the corruption investigations he faces at home, and whether Washington is done with the Bolsonaros.

intro.plain: Big news out of Brazil and Washington. Flávio Bolsonaro lost the presidential runoff to Lula, says the vote was stolen, and is now in the United States. Sources say Trump is not planning to back his claim to lead Brazil. Chat: should the US recognise a result its ally disputes, or stay out of it?
intro.mid: Flávio Bolsonaro lost to Lula in the second round, called it fraud, and left for America. He was counting on Trump. Sources now say Trump will not back him, and Democrats in Congress want to know why he is here at all. With his immunity running out next year, what does he do now? Chat, tell me.
intro.bold: Lose the election, call it stolen, leave the country. Flávio Bolsonaro just ran the family playbook, and this time Trump reportedly is not playing along. He faces corruption investigations at home and a probe in Congress here. Chat: is Bolsonaro a persecuted leader or a man running from the law?

hook.plain: Flávio Bolsonaro lost Brazil's presidential runoff and left for the United States. Now sources say Trump will not back his claim to lead Brazil. Here is why.
hook.mid: He called Brazil's election stolen and counted on Trump to say so too. Sources say that is not happening. Here is what comes next.
hook.bold: Flávio Bolsonaro lost, cried fraud and fled to America. Then his strongest ally stepped back. Here is why he is suddenly on his own.
